blueprint_concepts: Distance of a point from a line, distance between parallel lines

concept_use.Distance of a point from a line, distanc: The distance between the parallel tangents (after normalising 6x-8y-30=0) gives the diameter 4 and the mid-parallel for the centre.
concept_use.Intercepts of a circle: The intercept formulas 2 sqrt(r^2-k^2) on the x-axis and 2 sqrt(r^2-h^2) on the y-axis fix k and give the answer.

english: A circle $C$ touches each of the lines $3x-4y+5=0$ and $6x-8y-30=0$, cuts off a chord of length $2\sqrt3$ on the $x$-axis and meets the $y$-axis. Then the length of the chord that $C$ cuts off on the $y$-axis is
hindi: एक वृत्त $C$ प्रत्येक रेखा $3x-4y+5=0$ तथा $6x-8y-30=0$ को स्पर्श करता है, $x$-अक्ष पर $2\sqrt3$ लम्बाई की जीवा काटता है तथा $y$-अक्ष से मिलता है। तब $C$ द्वारा $y$-अक्ष पर काटी गई जीवा की लम्बाई है
solution: Second line: $3x-4y-15=0$, parallel to the first; distance between them $=\dfrac{|5+15|}{5}=4$
A circle touching two parallel lines has diameter $4$, so $r=2$, and its centre $(h,k)$ is on the mid-parallel $3x-4y-5=0$
$k=1\Rightarrow h=3$: $|h|>r$, the circle misses the $y$-axis; $k=-1\Rightarrow h=\dfrac13$
solution_full: Divide the second line by $2$: $3x-4y-15=0$. It is parallel to $3x-4y+5=0$, so the circle lies between two parallel lines and touches both.
Distance between the parallel lines $=\dfrac{|5-(-15)|}{\sqrt{9+16}}=4$. A circle touching both has this distance as a diameter, so $r=2$.
Its centre $(h,k)$ is equidistant from the two lines, so it lies on the mid-parallel $3x-4y+\dfrac{5-15}{2}=0$, i.e. $3x-4y-5=0$.
The chord on the $x$-axis has length $2\sqrt{r^2-k^2}$ (here $|k|$ is the distance of the centre from the $x$-axis). So $2\sqrt{4-k^2}=2\sqrt3\Rightarrow k^2=1$.
Case $k=1$: $3h-4-5=0\Rightarrow h=3$. The distance of the centre from the $y$-axis is $3>2=r$, so this circle does not meet the $y$-axis; it is rejected.
Case $k=-1$: $3h+4-5=0\Rightarrow h=\dfrac13$. Here $|h|<r$, so the circle meets the $y$-axis.
$C:\left(x-\frac13\right)^2+(y+1)^2=4$. Its chord on the $y$-axis has length $2\sqrt{r^2-h^2}=2\sqrt{4-\frac19}=2\sqrt{\frac{35}{9}}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{35}}{3}$.
originality_note: New: two parallel tangents written with different scalings fix the radius and the locus of the centre, an x-intercept fixes two candidate circles, and the condition 'meets the y-axis' selects one (way 3: object fixed by two conditions plus a selection). Closest known: circle touching two parallel lines with centre on a given line. Different because: the centre is located through an intercept condition and one candidate must be rejected because its y-intercept is not real.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. The second line is deliberately not normalised; checked that the two candidate circles are distinct and only one meets the y-axis. Changed: added 'meets the y-axis' to make C unique.
key_step: Radius from the distance between parallel lines, centre on the mid-parallel, then rejecting the candidate circle that misses the y-axis.
justification: Several standard results chained with a normalisation trap and a case rejection; each step is routine but two conditions must be combined and one case discarded. Similar in demand to 2021-P1-Q1 (L3), a circle located from line conditions.
